beats.head: Boreas Power Seals $6.8B Third Anchor Pact, Cementing Coast-to-Coast Campus Grid
beats.body: Mira Thorne's acquisitive streak reached a new peak with a $6.8B third anchor supply pact that links the eastern and western campus networks into a single coast-to-coast grid. The deal brings total committed campus supply above $16B across three anchors in under two years. Thorne told TNN the network is now 'the backbone we always intended to build, not a collection of sites.'

beats.head: Castlestone Surges as Grid-Core Ascend Framework Drives Record Compute Quarter
beats.body: Castlestone completed its turnaround with a blowout quarter, as the $6.1B multi-region framework drove compute revenue up 71% year-over-year. CEO Pell Karsh, who staked his tenure on the Grid-Core Ascend line, said the platform is now shipping across four regions with a second framework in negotiation. The result fully reverses the earlier ramp-cost overrun that had dogged the launch.

beats.head: Drayton Freight Beats and Raises Again as Expanded Automation Contract Books Fully
beats.body: Drayton Freight topped estimates and lifted full-year guidance as the $420M expansion to its warehouse automation contract began booking alongside the base $900M program. CEO Emil Holt said material handling utilization hit a company record during the quarter. The combined contract is now Drayton's largest ever, representing over a third of annual revenue.

beats.head: Drossware Extends Reformulation Push Into Packaging With Recyclable Line
beats.body: Building on the success of its overhauled cleaning range, Drossware introduced a new fully recyclable packaging line under CEO Nadia Wold. The rollout covers 40 formats across food and consumer segments, with two anchor retail partners already committed to phased adoption. Wold framed the launch as 'the natural next step after cleaning proved the model works.'

beats.head: Dunmorestone Edges Past Estimates as Restaurant Contract Reaches Full Ramp
beats.body: Dunmorestone posted a modest quarterly beat as its multi-site restaurant group contract reached full deployment across food service and fixtures. CEO Orla Mercer noted the fixtures expansion is now running at roughly 90% utilization. Margins held steady, with management reaffirming full-year guidance.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Wins Second Meridian Framework as Corvalan's Bet Gains Traction
beats.body: Halhold Systems secured a second major Meridian compute framework valued at $1.9B, extending the momentum CEO Ines Corvalan built after returning the company to profit. The order doubles Meridian's committed pipeline and pulls forward capacity plans by two quarters. Corvalan cautioned that scaling delivery 'will test our operations,' a nod to the turbulence that has marked her tenure.

beats.head: Hesperforge Supply Breaks Ground on Fifth Mill as Marine Backlog Tops $2B
beats.body: CEO Sable Halloran committed $510M to a fifth mill at the company's Harroway complex, citing a marine framework backlog that has now climbed past $2B. The facility is expected to add roughly 18% to structural materials capacity when it reaches full output in late 1915. Halloran called the move 'a measured bet on demand we can already see on the order book.'

beats.head: Korrwright Works Debuts First Timepiece Built on Newly Acquired Dovreux Cases
beats.body: Just months after the $620M Dovreux Frères deal, CEO Dunmore Carrow unveiled the Halbrook Meridian, the first Korrwright piece using in-house-controlled Dovreux casework. The limited run of 300 carries a list price near $148,000 and showcases the vertical integration Carrow promised at acquisition. Early allocations to Verenne dealers sold through within days.

beats.head: Brunforge Holdings Beats as Third Vellan Wave Lifts Flagship Contribution
beats.body: Brunforge Holdings topped estimates with revenue of $1.42B versus the $1.36B consensus, as the third Vellan wave pushed its flagship count past forty and drove device and fine-goods sales. CEO Kestrel Bramm said mature first-wave stores are now delivering full-year contributions while newer flagships ramp. Operating margin expanded to 11.8%.

beats.head: Drustcraft Wins $260M Fasteners Supply Deal, Broadening Beyond Auto Parts
beats.body: Drustcraft secured a $260M three-year fasteners and fixings supply agreement with a regional appliance maker, deepening its second product line beyond the auto-parts pact now ramping across three lines. CEO Cora Fenn called the award a deliberate step to balance the business, adding that the fasteners line will add a fourth shift to meet volumes. The deal lifts committed backlog to roughly $840M.

beats.head: Marrowstone Build Unveils Next-Gen Excavator Line to Serve Rail Backlog
beats.body: Marrowstone Build introduced its Vantage series of earthmoving machines, a lineup of four excavator and grader models built for the heavy grading demands of its coastal rail and highway work. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the fleet will first deploy on the $780M Coastal Rail Corridor, with the company committing $95M to retool its assembly hall in Marrowstone. The launch marks the firm's first major equipment refresh in six years.

beats.head: Skarngrove & Sons Beats as Vantry Junction Ramps and Kelvarn Tails Off
beats.body: Skarngrove & Sons posted quarterly revenue of $612M, ahead of the $580M consensus, as the Vantry Rail Junction order began contributing while the winding-down Kelvarn corridor delivered final billings. CEO Quinn Fenn credited disciplined sequencing of the two programs for holding margins at 14.2%. Backlog closed the quarter at $1.9B.

beats.head: Stegreach Lands $1.1B Grid-Modernization Framework, Its Largest Ever
beats.body: Stegreach secured a five-year, $1.1B framework agreement to supply fasteners, lighting, and wire and cable across a nationwide substation upgrade program, dwarfing its recent Riverport awards. CEO Halden Ashby called the deal a defining moment, noting it locks in three of the company's four product lines through 2031 and roughly doubles its committed forward workload. The award follows two years of steady Riverport grid wins that positioned Stegreach as the preferred supplier.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Wins $1.9B Fleet Order as Veyra Turnaround Lands Its Biggest Prize Yet
beats.body: Brunmark Motors secured a $1.9B multi-year contract to supply Veyra vehicles and Power & Storage packs to national logistics operator Halden Freightways. CEO Iris Calvagh called the deal 'the proof point the reset was built for,' with first deliveries slated within eight months. The order roughly doubles Brunmark's commercial backlog and marks the largest single win in Calvagh's tenure.

beats.head: Veldtreach & Sons Awarded $1.2B Inland Reservoir Expansion in Signature Steg Bet
beats.body: Veldtreach & Sons won the prime contract for Phase II of the Coldwater Basin reservoir program, valued at $1.2B over four years. CEO Petra Steg said the win vindicates the earlier decision to commission a fourth earthmoving fleet ahead of demand. The award nearly triples the firm's reservoir-related backlog and secures work through the decade's end.

beats.head: Fennmoor Strikes $3.4B Merger to Fold Machine-Tool Giant Voight Into Industrial Arm
beats.body: Chairman Dorian Brandt, now in his sixth decade at the helm, announced the largest acquisition in company history, absorbing precision machine-tool maker Voight to bolster Fennmoor's Industrial Machines division. The cash-and-stock deal follows the successful integration of Halquist and Carrow, and Brandt said it would lift industrial revenue past the medical segment for the first time. Regulators are expected to review the tie-up over the coming months.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Faces New Regulatory Probe as Storage-Bank Fault Spreads to Field Units
beats.body: Regulators opened a fresh inquiry after reports of thermal faults in deployed storage banks, widening the scope of the crisis that toppled Corin Alderidge. CEO Maren Vok ordered a voluntary field inspection of some 12,000 installed units and set aside $220M for remediation. The disclosure lands atop the pending $1.6B investor suit, deepening pressure on Vok's turnaround.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Faces Formal Investigation as Regulators Seize Emberline Records
beats.body: Authorities opened a formal safety-records probe into the Emberline fabrication site after evidence that inspection logs had been altered, ordering the seizure of internal documents and interviews with plant leadership. Marisol Venn placed two site executives on leave and suspended a portion of Emberline output pending review, warning of possible near-term shipment delays. The company disclosed it is cooperating fully but declined to quantify the financial impact.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Posts Steep Loss as Discharge Fallout Erases Compute Revenue
beats.body: The crisis chief's first report revealed a quarterly loss of $410M as the collapsed $2.4B compute pact and departing customers gutted revenue, which fell 38% year over year. The company took additional charges tied to the discharge restatement and warned of continued cash burn while the partner lawsuit proceeds. Management withdrew forward guidance, citing 'unresolved litigation and rebuilding trust.'

beats.head: Korrwright Group Wins $3.4B Transit Corridor Contract in Largest Award in Its History
beats.body: Halden Fenn secured the multi-year Eastreach Corridor package, supplying structural materials and wire & cable for a regional rail and utility spine. The award, worth $3.4B over six years, arrives just as Harbor redevelopment billing peaks, giving Korrwright a rare double-anchor backlog. Fenn said the win 'extends visibility well into the next decade' and lifts total backlog past $9B.

beats.head: Castlestone Vindicates Karsh as Grid-Core Ascend Wins $6.1B Multi-Region Compute Framework
beats.body: Castlestone secured a $6.1 billion, five-year framework agreement to supply Grid-Core Ascend compute across three national infrastructure programs, its largest single award on record. CEO Pell Karsh, who staked his comeback on the line despite a bruising ramp-cost overrun last quarter, said the deal validates the bet and locks in demand through 2031. Management now expects Ascend margins to turn positive by the second half as volume absorbs fixed costs.

beats.head: Gromford Works Sued Over Emblem Signature Sourcing Claims as Regulators Join Prestige Probe
beats.body: A coalition of luxury retailers filed suit against Gromford Works, alleging the Emblem Signature editions were marketed with provenance claims the company could not substantiate, seeking damages and rescinded contracts. A market-conduct regulator confirmed a parallel inquiry into Gromford's sourcing disclosures. CEO Halvard Pryce, whose rapid prestige push drove the line's launch, said the company 'stands behind Emblem' but has suspended new Signature shipments pending review.
